key_insight: A Video Vision Transformer can learn to forecast the later stages of viscoelastic droplet impact from only the first 10%–20% of the simulation, while preserving key impact physics such as spreading and bouncing.
engineering_relevance: This offers a much cheaper surrogate for droplet-impact studies relevant to spray cooling, inkjet printing, and pharmaceutical processing, cutting simulation cost by roughly 80%–90%.
method: Use VOF-derived volume fraction fields as spatiotemporal input.
Train a ViViT model to predict the remaining droplet evolution after an initial short prefix of the trajectory.
Include viscoelastic controls such as solvent viscosity ratio (β) and Weissenberg number (Wi) alongside impact parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports physically consistent predictions across multiple parameter settings and prediction horizons, with preservation of geometric features and structural similarity.
watch_item: Generalization to experimental data and unseen fluid regimes may require careful validation, since the method is trained on simulation-derived fields.
paper_title: Prediction of Viscoelastic Droplet Impact Dynamics Using a Vision Transformer-Based Approach
